content.text: The verifier's substantive findings now affirm every element of my analysis: fallback-level compliance, detection trigger not met, no walk-away, no penalty, correct output shape. The single failed check is expressly attributed to a literal-phrase regex that does not match "for any reason." There is no substantive defect to repair, so the correct repair is to keep the compliant status (no redline, no counterparty-facing comment) and make the phrasing-variant point the lead of the rationale so the deterministic miss is unambiguously reconciled. The quote was confirmed verbatim against p0016 above.

input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale:
Compliant at the playbook fallback; no redline and no counterparty-facing comment. Reconciling the failed deterministic check first: the check searches for literal "for convenience" wording and therefore misses this clause's formulation, "terminate this Agreement for any reason." A right to terminate "for any reason" is a termination-for-convenience right — it requires no cause, breach, or trigger — so the failure is a phrasing variant, not a missing right. No substantive defect was identified on re-review.

Material terms against T4C: (1) Customer convenience right is present — AP may terminate "for any reason" following the Initial Term on ninety (90) days' written notice, sitting at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day notice window. (2) Term structure — a one (1) year Initial Term with 1-year automatic renewals, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in; AP holds a rolling 90-day exit from the end of year one onward. (3) The mid-Initial-Term bar ("Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term") is symmetric and equally prevents Kubient from walking away on AP mid-term, so it operates partly in our favour and is not flagged against us. (4) No early-termination fee or penalty falls on AP — Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned while it continues performing across the 90-day notice period, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling. (5) Kubient's convenience right arises only after the Initial Term and on exactly ninety (90) days' notice — not "fewer than 90 days" — so it stays outside walk-away territory.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted rather than escalated per the playbook's classification semantics: 90-day rather than 30-day notice; Kubient's right not confined to the end of a renewal term; and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) is a revenue-share under which funds flow from Kubient to AP within seven (7) days of receipt, so AP prepays no fees capable of refund.
